The main sources of added phosphorus were cheese, soft drinks, cakes/pies, rolls/buns, and cookies/brownies (Fulgoni and Fulgoni,
2021). With this approach, it may be easier to estimate total phosphorus intake and associate it with health outcomes.
Absorption
Phosphorus absorption in adults and children is very efﬁcient (65–75%) and an increase in serum phosphorus can be observed
within an hour after ingestion of a meal begins.
Absorption of dietary phosphate occurs in the gastrointestinal tract through at least two pathways: the transcellular, sodium-
dependent pathway, and the paracellular, sodium-independent pathway. The main apical intestinal transporter in the transcellular
absorption of phosphorus is the sodium-dependent phosphate cotransporter 2b (NaPi-2b), which is believed to be responsible for
absorption when dietary phosphorus is low (Saurette and Alexander, 2019; Fishban and Nigwekar, 2021). The transporter NaPi-2b
is highly regulated by the expression of calcitriol (1,25 (OH)2D3) and by dietary phosphorus levels. For instance, when phosphorus
